the current data, both from flavour physics and direct LHC searches, have a limited impact on the parameter space of supersymmetry.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the LHC has been very successful in probing new physics at high energy scales, but it is still not competitive with flavour measurements for probing low energy scales.
, at the current level of precision, the LHC is not able to probe the flavour sector in the MSSM.
the current status of LHC searches for new physics is still not enough to exclude the supersymmetric models based on U(2).
The main takeaway from our work is that
the LHC is already probing the parameter space of flavour symmetries in the quark and lepton sectors, and that it will be the most important tool to probe flavour physics in the coming years.
